wave: DOCUMENTATION-TRACKS-IMPLEMENTATION -- ROADMAP.md understated R4 status by three whole dimensions
wave_title: `.atlas/roadmap/ROADMAP.md`'s R4 summary line read 'Current materialized baseline is R4.8 bootstrap', and R4.9 (Ownership)/R4.10 (Concurrency)/R4.11 (Persistence) were listed with plain, unmarked descriptions implying not-yet-started -- while `adapter::semantic::rust::SUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS` has long included all twelve R4 dimensions, and real, substantial extractor files (ownership.rs, concurrency.rs, persistence.rs, 273-335 lines each, each explicitly self-labeled 'R4.9'/'R4.10'/'R4.11' in their own module doc comments) implement them. The repository's own more detailed status record, `.atlas/roadmap/SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md`, already correctly described all three as 'bootstrap materialized, closure remains open' -- ROADMAP.md's own summary table had simply not been kept in sync with it.

generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct inspection of the repository's own roadmap after three consecutive investigation-focused generations found no new mandatory code-level gap, per the standing loop's own instruction to check whether R4 has 'closed' before continuing rather than inventing further ad hoc bug hunts. Reading ROADMAP.md's R4 section literally (not from memory) surfaced the discrepancy: R4.4 through R4.8 each carry an explicit completion marker ('materialized:' or 'bootstrap materialized, closure open'), while R4.9/R4.10/R4.11 carried none at all -- read literally, this implies they had not started. Cross-checked directly against the real code (`SUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS`, `dimension_coverage`, and each extractor file's own module doc comment, which self-labels its own R-number) and against the OTHER canonical roadmap document (`SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md`), which already had the correct, detailed, accurate status for all three -- confirming ROADMAP.md specifically (not the underlying implementation or the other doc) was the stale artifact.

priority_classification: documentation-tracks-implementation (the standing loop's own explicit requirement: 'Documentation must track implementation in the same coherent change... never claim capabilities the code lacks'). This is the inverse direction of that same principle -- the code has capabilities the summary roadmap document did not credit it with -- which is just as much a documentation-integrity defect as overclaiming: a reader of ROADMAP.md alone (without also reading the more detailed SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md) would incorrectly believe three real, substantial, tested capabilities do not exist yet.

design_decisions.question: Mark R4.9/10/11 with the same unqualified 'materialized:' label used for R4.4-R4.7, or the more precise 'bootstrap materialized, closure remains open' label already used for R4.8?
design_decisions.decision: 'Bootstrap materialized, closure remains open' -- matching both R4.8's own existing label in this same document and, more importantly, matching `SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md`'s own already-correct, more detailed status for exactly these three items. Per the standing loop's own instruction to use existing repository vocabulary rather than inventing competing terms, and to distinguish specified/scaffolded/materialized/verified/closed precisely: R4.9/10/11 are real and typed (not mere stubs) but every one of them is `DimensionCoverage::Partial`, the identical completion class R4.8 is already labeled with -- using the plain, unqualified 'materialized:' label (implying a closure level equivalent to R4.4's declaration-level Exhaustive coverage) would overclaim in the other direction.

design_decisions.question: Rewrite SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md too, since it's the more detailed record?
design_decisions.decision: No changes needed there -- it was already correct. This generation's fix is entirely to ROADMAP.md's own summary table and lead sentence, which is the one place found to disagree with both the real code and the repository's own more detailed status document.
